newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo to target telecoms, farms, roads.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo to target telecoms, farms, roads.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's Congo plans to target telecommunications, farming and road building as priorities as it attempts to rebuild its war-ravaged economy.

Finance Minister Mawapanga Mwana Nanga told reporters that the mineral-rich former Zaire, renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo, would encourage competition and foreign involvement in the telecoms sector and offer incentives for investment in farming.

"We will have a conference on telecommunications in September. We will use the same competition philosophy to bring big telecommunication companies which can come and make the telephone not a luxury but something everyone can afford," Mawapanga said.
Zaire's traditional source of wealth is minerals such as copper, cobalt, diamonds and gold.
Kabila's government struck deals with some foreign mining companies before taking power in May. It has spoken of linking other mining deals to barter-style infrastructure projects.

Basic infrastructure is in tatters after decades of corruption and neglect under ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko, toppled by Kabila's forces two months ago. Mobutu fled leaving Africa's third largest nation facing economic ruin, with a foreign debt of $14 billion.
The state telephone network is in a state of almost terminal decline.

The nation relies on cellular telephones introduced by Telecel, a local company with American shareholders. But high fees mean Telecel can count only 11,000 subscribers in a nation of over 40 million people. Comcell, a rival phone company owned by a Mobutu ally, was not as successful as Telecel but the authorities are keen to foster competition.
"In a few months, in a few years, Telecel will no longer be the only player on the market," Mawapanga said.

He said that the promotion of agriculture was also one of the government's priorities. "We will try to bring in investors. Those who will invest in agriculture will get incentives, tax-breaks for instance," he said.
Kabila also wants to promote road building.

"The president says we need to rebuild about 500 km of paved road per province. We cannot exclude certain provinces and give priority to other provinces. We want all our people to feel the benefit of the liberation," Mawapanga said.

"We will move aggressively to try to improve infrastructure all over the country. Even in places you think there is nothing in this deep forest you may go and find the biggest goldmine that has ever existed," he added.
He did not say where the funding would come from.
Mobutu is said to have stashed away billions of dollars. The government wants the alleged fortune back home but Mawapanga said the problem was in the hands of the judiciary.
"If we get money from Mobutu's assets, it will be a windfall. It will help us pay the debt and have our people back at work. But before we get that, we are not going to sit and wait," he said.
